datasets.name: ds_signals
queryLines:
WITH anchor AS (SELECT max(event_time) AS t FROM audit),
sig AS (
  SELECT rule, actor, event_time,
         first(stage) AS stage, first(actor_kind) AS actor_kind, first(nullif(src_ip, '')) AS src_ip,
         coalesce(first(actor_name), actor) AS actor_name, first(summary) AS summary
  FROM demo_signals CROSS JOIN anchor
  WHERE created_at >= anchor.t AND event_time >= anchor.t - INTERVAL 1 DAY
  GROUP BY rule, actor, event_time
),
sig_named AS (
  SELECT *, CASE stage WHEN '1' THEN '1 Access' WHEN '2' THEN '2 Discovery' WHEN '3' THEN '3 Secret harvest' WHEN '4' THEN '4 Execution' WHEN '5' THEN '5 Persistence' WHEN '6' THEN '6 Collection and clean-up' WHEN 'corr' THEN 'Correlation' ELSE 'Other' END AS stage_label,
         CASE WHEN startswith(rule, 'ada_') THEN 'Stage rules (ada_)' ELSE 'Single-event rules (adp_)' END AS family
  FROM sig
)
SELECT event_time, rule, family, stage_label AS stage, actor, actor_name, actor_kind,
       coalesce(src_ip, '') AS src_ip, summary,
       CASE WHEN family = 'Stage rules (ada_)' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_ada,
       CASE WHEN family = 'Single-event rules (adp_)' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_adp,
       CASE WHEN family = 'Stage rules (ada_)' THEN actor END AS ada_actor
FROM sig_named
ORDER BY event_time

datasets.name: ds_timeline
queryLines:
WITH anchor AS (SELECT max(event_time) AS t FROM audit),
sig AS (
  SELECT rule, actor, event_time,
         first(stage) AS stage, first(actor_kind) AS actor_kind, first(nullif(src_ip, '')) AS src_ip,
         coalesce(first(actor_name), actor) AS actor_name, first(summary) AS summary
  FROM demo_signals CROSS JOIN anchor
  WHERE created_at >= anchor.t AND event_time >= anchor.t - INTERVAL 1 DAY
  GROUP BY rule, actor, event_time
),
sig_named AS (
  SELECT *, CASE stage WHEN '1' THEN '1 Access' WHEN '2' THEN '2 Discovery' WHEN '3' THEN '3 Secret harvest' WHEN '4' THEN '4 Execution' WHEN '5' THEN '5 Persistence' WHEN '6' THEN '6 Collection and clean-up' WHEN 'corr' THEN 'Correlation' ELSE 'Other' END AS stage_label,
         CASE WHEN startswith(rule, 'ada_') THEN 'Stage rules (ada_)' ELSE 'Single-event rules (adp_)' END AS family
  FROM sig
),
ada AS (SELECT * FROM sig_named WHERE family = 'Stage rules (ada_)'),
shared_ips AS (SELECT src_ip FROM ada WHERE src_ip IS NOT NULL GROUP BY src_ip HAVING count(DISTINCT actor) > 1),
lanes AS (
  SELECT a.actor_name AS lane, 'identity' AS lane_kind, a.event_time, a.stage_label, a.rule, a.src_ip,
         a.actor_name, a.summary, s.src_ip IS NOT NULL AS on_shared_ip
  FROM ada a LEFT JOIN shared_ips s ON s.src_ip = a.src_ip
  UNION ALL
  SELECT concat('IP ', a.src_ip), 'shared IP', a.event_time, a.stage_label, a.rule, a.src_ip, a.actor_name,
         a.summary, true
  FROM ada a JOIN shared_ips s ON s.src_ip = a.src_ip
),
-- Lane order: the identities that share an IP first, then that IP, then the rest by their first signal.
ordered AS (
  SELECT *, min(event_time) OVER (PARTITION BY lane) AS lane_start,
         CASE WHEN lane_kind = 'shared IP' THEN 1
              WHEN max(on_shared_ip) OVER (PARTITION BY lane) THEN 0
              ELSE 2 END AS lane_group
  FROM lanes
)
SELECT lane, lane_kind, event_time, stage_label AS stage, rule, src_ip, actor_name, summary,
       dense_rank() OVER (ORDER BY lane_group, lane_start, lane) AS lane_order
FROM ordered
ORDER BY event_time

datasets.name: ds_contrast
queryLines:
WITH anchor AS (SELECT max(event_time) AS t FROM audit),
sig AS (
  SELECT rule, actor, event_time,
         first(stage) AS stage, first(actor_kind) AS actor_kind, first(nullif(src_ip, '')) AS src_ip,
         coalesce(first(actor_name), actor) AS actor_name, first(summary) AS summary
  FROM demo_signals CROSS JOIN anchor
  WHERE created_at >= anchor.t AND event_time >= anchor.t - INTERVAL 1 DAY
  GROUP BY rule, actor, event_time
),
sig_named AS (
  SELECT *, CASE stage WHEN '1' THEN '1 Access' WHEN '2' THEN '2 Discovery' WHEN '3' THEN '3 Secret harvest' WHEN '4' THEN '4 Execution' WHEN '5' THEN '5 Persistence' WHEN '6' THEN '6 Collection and clean-up' WHEN 'corr' THEN 'Correlation' ELSE 'Other' END AS stage_label,
         CASE WHEN startswith(rule, 'ada_') THEN 'Stage rules (ada_)' ELSE 'Single-event rules (adp_)' END AS family
  FROM sig
),
grps AS (
  SELECT * FROM VALUES
    (1, 'S1 attack: Maria Lopez', 'Maria Lopez'),
    (2, 'S1 attack: sp-etl-prod', 'sp-etl-prod'),
    (3, 'S2 attack: sp-reporting', 'sp-reporting'),
    (4, 'S3 attack: Tom Becker', 'Tom Becker'),
    (5, 'S4 attack: sp-ml-batch', 'sp-ml-batch'),
    (6, 'D1 decoy: sp-ci-deploy', 'sp-ci-deploy'),
    (7, 'D2 decoy: Ana Silva', 'Ana Silva'),
    (8, 'Background (all other identities)', CAST(NULL AS STRING))
  AS g(ord, grp, display_name)
),
members AS (SELECT g.ord, p.email FROM grps g JOIN principals p ON p.display_name = g.display_name),
fired AS (SELECT DISTINCT s.rule, trim(a) AS actor FROM sig_named s LATERAL VIEW explode(split(s.actor, ',')) x AS a),
hits AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT coalesce(m.ord, 8) AS ord, f.rule
  FROM fired f LEFT JOIN members m ON m.email = f.actor
),
fam AS (SELECT * FROM VALUES ('Stage rules (ada_)', 'ada_'), ('Single-event rules (adp_)', 'adp_') AS f(family, prefix))
SELECT g.ord, g.grp, f.family, count(h.rule) AS rules
FROM grps g CROSS JOIN fam f LEFT JOIN hits h ON h.ord = g.ord AND startswith(h.rule, f.prefix)
GROUP BY g.ord, g.grp, f.family
ORDER BY g.ord, f.family

datasets.name: ds_actions
queryLines:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT a.event_time, a.user_identity.email AS actor,
         coalesce(p.display_name, a.user_identity.email) AS actor_name, a.source_ip_address AS src_ip,
         a.service_name, a.action_name, a.response.status_code AS status, a.user_agent, a.request_params
  FROM audit a LEFT JOIN principals p ON p.email = a.user_identity.email
  WHERE a.event_time >= (SELECT max(event_time) FROM audit) - INTERVAL 24 HOURS
)
SELECT event_time, actor, actor_name, src_ip, service_name, action_name, status, user_agent,
       to_json(request_params) AS request_params,
       timestamp_seconds(floor(unix_timestamp(event_time) / 600) * 600) AS ten_minutes
FROM base
WHERE (:actor = 'All' OR actor_name = :actor) AND (:ip = 'All' OR src_ip = :ip)
ORDER BY event_time DESC
LIMIT 20000

datasets.name: ds_identities
queryLines:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT a.event_time, a.user_identity.email AS actor,
         coalesce(p.display_name, a.user_identity.email) AS actor_name, a.source_ip_address AS src_ip,
         a.service_name, a.action_name, a.response.status_code AS status, a.user_agent, a.request_params
  FROM audit a LEFT JOIN principals p ON p.email = a.user_identity.email
  WHERE a.event_time >= (SELECT max(event_time) FROM audit) - INTERVAL 24 HOURS
)
SELECT identity FROM (
  SELECT 'All' AS identity, 0 AS o
  UNION ALL
  SELECT DISTINCT actor_name, 1 FROM base WHERE actor_name IS NOT NULL
)
ORDER BY o, identity

datasets.name: ds_ips
queryLines:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT a.event_time, a.user_identity.email AS actor,
         coalesce(p.display_name, a.user_identity.email) AS actor_name, a.source_ip_address AS src_ip,
         a.service_name, a.action_name, a.response.status_code AS status, a.user_agent, a.request_params
  FROM audit a LEFT JOIN principals p ON p.email = a.user_identity.email
  WHERE a.event_time >= (SELECT max(event_time) FROM audit) - INTERVAL 24 HOURS
)
SELECT ip FROM (
  SELECT 'All' AS ip, 0 AS o
  UNION ALL
  SELECT DISTINCT src_ip, 1 FROM base WHERE src_ip IS NOT NULL
)
ORDER BY o, ip

queryLines:
WITH anchor AS (SELECT max(event_time) AS t FROM audit),
sig AS (
  SELECT rule, actor, event_time,
         first(stage) AS stage, first(actor_kind) AS actor_kind, first(nullif(src_ip, '')) AS src_ip,
         coalesce(first(actor_name), actor) AS actor_name, first(summary) AS summary
  FROM demo_signals CROSS JOIN anchor
  WHERE created_at >= anchor.t AND event_time >= anchor.t - INTERVAL 1 DAY
  GROUP BY rule, actor, event_time
),
sig_named AS (
  SELECT *, CASE stage WHEN '1' THEN '1 Access' WHEN '2' THEN '2 Discovery' WHEN '3' THEN '3 Secret harvest' WHEN '4' THEN '4 Execution' WHEN '5' THEN '5 Persistence' WHEN '6' THEN '6 Collection and clean-up' WHEN 'corr' THEN 'Correlation' ELSE 'Other' END AS stage_label,
         CASE WHEN startswith(rule, 'ada_') THEN 'Stage rules (ada_)' ELSE 'Single-event rules (adp_)' END AS family
  FROM sig
)
SELECT event_time, rule, stage_label AS stage, actor_name, coalesce(src_ip, '') AS src_ip, summary

datasets.name: ds_h6b_chain
queryLines:
SELECT chain, src_ip, reader_name, first_read_at, last_read_at, array_join(secrets_read, ', ') AS secrets_read,
       denied_reads, sp_name, sp_auth_at, sp_user_agent, first_priv_at, last_priv_at,
       array_join(sp_actions, ', ') AS sp_actions
FROM (
WITH ev AS (
  SELECT event_time, user_identity.email AS actor, source_ip_address AS src_ip, user_agent, action_name,
         request_params.scope AS scope, request_params.key AS key, response.status_code AS status,
         CASE WHEN user_identity.email RLIKE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$'
                OR identity_metadata.acting_resource_type ILIKE '%service principal%'
              THEN 'sp' ELSE 'user' END AS actor_kind
  FROM audit
  WHERE event_time >= (SELECT max(event_time) FROM audit)
                      - INTERVAL 24 HOURS
    AND source_ip_address IS NOT NULL
    AND action_name IN ('getSecret', 'tokenLogin', 'oidcTokenAuthorization',
                        'createFunction', 'addPrincipalToGroup', 'generateDbToken', 'workspaceExport')
)
SELECT concat(pr.display_name, ' -> ', ps.display_name) AS chain, m.src_ip, m.readers[0] AS reader, pr.display_name AS reader_name, m.first_read_at, m.last_read_at,
       m.secrets_read, m.denied_reads, m.sp, ps.display_name AS sp_name, m.sp_auth_at, m.sp_user_agent,
       m.first_priv_at, m.last_priv_at, m.sp_actions
FROM ev
MATCH_RECOGNIZE (
  PARTITION BY src_ip
  ORDER BY event_time
  MEASURES collect_set(get_secret.actor) AS readers,
           FIRST(get_secret.event_time) AS first_read_at,
           LAST(get_secret.event_time) AS last_read_at,
           collect_set(concat(get_secret.scope, '/', get_secret.key)) AS secrets_read,
           count_if(get_secret.status <> 200) AS denied_reads,
           FIRST(sp_auth.actor) AS sp,
           FIRST(sp_auth.event_time) AS sp_auth_at,
           FIRST(sp_auth.user_agent) AS sp_user_agent,
           FIRST(sp_priv.event_time) AS first_priv_at,
           LAST(sp_priv.event_time) AS last_priv_at,
           collect_list(sp_priv.action_name) AS sp_actions
  ONE ROW PER MATCH
  AFTER MATCH SKIP PAST LAST ROW
  PATTERN (get_secret+ other*? sp_auth sp_priv+)
  DEFINE get_secret AS action_name = 'getSecret',
         other      AS action_name <> 'getSecret'
                       AND NOT (actor_kind = 'sp' AND action_name IN ('tokenLogin', 'oidcTokenAuthorization')),
         sp_auth    AS action_name IN ('tokenLogin', 'oidcTokenAuthorization') AND status = 200
                       AND actor_kind = 'sp' AND actor <> LAST(get_secret.actor)
                       AND event_time <= LAST(get_secret.event_time) + INTERVAL 6 HOURS,
         sp_priv    AS action_name IN ('createFunction', 'addPrincipalToGroup', 'generateDbToken', 'workspaceExport')
                       AND actor = FIRST(sp_auth.actor)
) AS m
LEFT JOIN principals AS pr ON pr.email = m.readers[0]
LEFT JOIN principals AS ps ON ps.email = m.sp
ORDER BY m.first_read_at
) AS h6b
WHERE (:actor = 'All' OR :actor IN (reader_name, sp_name)) AND (:ip = 'All' OR src_ip = :ip)
ORDER BY first_read_at

## Databricks audit demo: one leaked token, two identities

An attacker uses a leaked personal access token (PAT) of a data engineer, reads the secret of a service principal, and continues as that service principal from the same IP. The data is a synthetic copy of `system.access.audit`; the signals are from the last reset of the demo.

frame.description: Rules that look for one step of an attack, or for a chain of steps

frame.title: Signals from single-event rules (adp_)
frame.description: Rules from the detection pack. They also fire on normal work

lines: **How to read this page.** Start with the top rows of the timeline: the PAT of Maria Lopez logs in from a new IP, lists resources and reads secrets. Then sp-etl-prod logs in from **the same IP** and creates functions, adds an admin, makes a token and exports a notebook. Each step alone looks like normal work; the order and the shared IP make it an attack. Open the **Investigate** page to see every action.

## Investigate an identity or an IP

Pick an identity or a source IP. The tables show the actions of the last 24 hours of the audit table and the signals of the last reset.
Tip: set Identity to **All** and pick the attacker IP to see **both** identities that used it.
